name: Furen's Armor
summary: In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard puts new armor to the test. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston for his trials. Furen then gives the fire-hardened mail to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths.

sections.title: A Master's Breakthrough
sections.body: Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, seeks stronger armor for the Alliance. He tests how well it withstands heat and crushing blows. For these trials, he asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials. The resulting mail succeeds, strengthening Furen's standing among Alliance armorers.

sections.title: Sharing the Craft
sections.body: Furen gives the finished fire-hardened mail to the warrior who gathered the materials. He is grateful for the help, and the experiments have deepened his knowledge of protective smithing. Now he plans to send his notes and findings to other Alliance smiths, so they can use the new methods.

faq.answer: Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer in Stormwind. He works extensively with the Alliance's martial orders, especially warriors seeking specialized armor.

faq.q: What kind of armor did Furen create?
faq.answer: Furen forged a Fire Hardened Hauberk, a mail chest piece made with rare fangs, horns, and phlogiston. It is built to withstand fierce attacks and extreme heat.

faq.q: Where does Furen Longbeard send his smithing discoveries?
faq.answer: Furen promises to send his findings and notes to fellow blacksmiths across the Alliance. He shares the tested tempering methods with forges throughout the realm.

faq.q: Why was the warrior asked to gather reagents for Furen?
faq.answer: Furen needed rare, volatile materials to test new smithing techniques. He could not leave his forge to hunt spiders in the Wetlands and chimaeras in Stonetalon, so he relied on an ambitious warrior to gather them.

faq.q: Where is this armor forged and delivered?
faq.answer: Furen forges and delivers the armor at his forge in Stormwind. There he completes the mail suit.

faq.q: Does this work benefit other Alliance fighters?
faq.answer: Yes. Furen plans to share what he learned with other Alliance armorers, hoping they will use the methods to make strong equipment for Alliance soldiers.

angles.text: As an Alliance warrior, you earn Furen's custom-tempered armor as you enter frontline service. It offers protection for early campaigns.
Furen's experiment shows how Alliance smiths share metallurgical findings to improve their craft in Stormwind and Ironforge.
Strong arms help keep Alliance forces alive against the Defias, gnolls, and hostile elemental forces.
